fields.concept_description: There is one of these for each classification applied to a legal entity. In this structure it names what a vehicle is for: management company, holding company, special purpose vehicle, tax blocker, fund vehicle or operating company. If you need to know which vehicles in a structure are tax blockers, this is what you go by. It is not a statement of what a body is to another, which comes from relationships.

There is one of these for each price of an instrument as at a date and of a given price type. In this structure it holds the fair value per unit of a private holding, with its level in the fair value hierarchy. If you need to value any fund's holding of an instrument, multiply the units it holds by this. It is not the amount a fund paid, which is held on the transaction.

There is one of these for each time money or a holding moved between parties in a single event, such as a capital call, a distribution, an acquisition, a follow-on investment, a partial or full exit, or a transfer to a continuation vehicle. If you need to know what happened on a date, what kind of event it was and who paid or received what, this is what you go by. It does not hold a fund's position, which is worked out from all of its transactions.

There is one of these for each valuation of a legal entity as at a date and on a named measure of value. In this structure it holds the net asset value of a fund and the equity value or enterprise value of a portfolio company or vehicle. If you need the value of a fund or a company at a reporting date, this is what you go by. A new valuation does not replace an earlier one, because each is kept for its own date. It is a view taken on a date and not a movement of money, so it is not a transaction. It is the value of the whole body and not the value of one fund's holding in it, which is the price per unit multiplied by the units held, and it is not the fair value of a single instrument, which is held with the instrument's price.

fields.relationship_description: A fund is managed by a general partner or manager for as long as the arrangement lasts, and a fund has one manager at a time, so the periods of its managers do not overlap. It holds the facts about the fund that belong to neither body alone: its vintage year, strategy, reporting currency, domicile, target size, final close date and the end of its investment period. If the manager of a fund is replaced, these facts are repeated on the new arrangement. It is not the fund's limited partners, who are linked by commitments.

A limited partner has committed capital to a fund for as long as the commitment runs. A limited partner may commit to several funds and a fund has many limited partners, and a second purchase of an existing interest is a further commitment of its own type. The amount, type and status belong to the commitment. It is not the money called or paid out, which is recorded as transactions.

A fund or vehicle holds a stake in a portfolio company or a holding vehicle for as long as it holds it. Several investors may hold one company and one investor may hold several. The economic share, voting share and control type belong to the stake. It is not what was paid for the stake, which is recorded as transactions.

Two funds or vehicles invest side by side, for example a main fund and its parallel fund, an alternative investment vehicle or a co-investment vehicle, for as long as they do. The kind of vehicle belongs to the link. It is not an investor's commitment to a fund.

A legal entity takes part in a transaction as a party to it, whether it pays or receives: the limited partner paying into a capital call, the fund receiving it, the fund paying for an acquisition, or the seller receiving the price. A transaction has several parties and a legal entity takes part in many transactions. Each party's record says whether it paid or received, the amount for each stated purpose and, where an instrument changed hands, the number of units. The date and currency belong to the transaction. It does not say which account the money passed through.
A transaction concerns one instrument, and many transactions may concern the same instrument. It names what was bought or sold. A capital call or distribution concerns no instrument.

A valuation judges the worth of one fund on a date and on a named measure, such as its net asset value. A fund is valued many times, once for each date and measure, and each valuation is about one fund. The date, amount, measure and currency belong to the valuation. It does not cover the value of a company the fund holds, which is linked to that company, nor the value of an instrument, which is held with the instrument's price, and it is not a transaction, because nothing is paid or received.

A valuation judges the worth of one portfolio company on a date and on a named measure, such as its equity value or enterprise value. A company is valued many times, once for each date and measure, and each valuation is about one company. The date, amount, measure and currency belong to the valuation. It does not cover the value of a fund, which is linked to the fund, nor the value of an instrument, which is held with the instrument's price, and it is not a transaction, because nothing is paid or received.

fields.attribute_description: The year in which the fund first took in investors' money. It is the year investors compare funds by, and it does not change after the first close.
The investment strategy the fund follows, taken from the agreed list. It says what kind of investing the fund does, not which industries it targets.
The currency in which the fund keeps its books and reports to investors.
The country in which the fund is established. Regulators ask for it, and it is not the country of the manager.
The amount of commitments the manager set out to raise for the fund, in the fund's reporting currency. It is not the commitments actually received.
The date on which the fund stopped accepting new investors. Investors who joined at earlier closes are measured from their own commitment dates.
The date on which the fund stops making new investments under its terms. Follow-on investments may continue after it.
How the holder relates to the company it has a stake in: control, joint control, significant influence or minority, taken from the agreed list.
The share of the company's economic value that the holder owns, as a percentage, for the period the stake was held. It is the percentage reported for the stake, not a figure added up over the chain.
The share of the company's votes the holder controls, as a percentage, where it differs from the economic share.
The kind of the side vehicle in the link: a parallel fund, an alternative investment vehicle or a co-investment vehicle. Where the link joins two funds of equal standing, it is a parallel fund.

The money this party paid or received in the transaction for the stated purpose, in the transaction's currency. A party taking part for several purposes has one amount for each. The side says whether it was paid or received.
The purpose for which this party paid or received, such as investment, management fee, fund expense, return of capital, realised gain or income, taken from the agreed list.
The number of units of the instrument this party received for its payment, or gave up for its receipt. It is blank for a capital call or a distribution.
What kind of event this was, such as a capital call, a distribution or an acquisition, taken from the agreed list.
The date on which the event took effect. Questions about what a fund held on a date use this date.
The date on which the money actually moved, where it differs from the date the event took effect.
The currency in which every amount on the transaction is stated, so that amounts paid and received by different parties can be added together.
Whether the transaction is active, still being drafted or no longer in force.
The date as at which the price applies. A price has no meaning without it.
The currency in which the price per unit of the instrument is stated, so that a price can be multiplied by a number of units without conversion.
The level of the fair value hierarchy the price falls in: Level 1, 2 or 3, according to how observable its inputs are.
The kind of price: a closing price or a fair value assessed at a reporting date.
The measure on which the value was struck, such as net asset value, equity value or enterprise value, taken from the agreed list. Two values on different measures are never compared as like for like.
The date as at which the valuation applies. A value has no meaning without the date it was struck, and later valuations do not replace earlier ones.
The value placed on the legal entity on the valuation date and measure, in the valuation currency.
The currency in which the valuation is stated, so that values struck at different dates can be compared.
Whether this party paid or received in the transaction, taken from the agreed list. It is what lets one relationship serve both sides of the movement.
